10-14: The Servant of God is born in Genoa. On the same day she is baptized and receives the name Rosa, Maria and Benedetta.
She writes that she is leaving but she would return to Piacenza on October 16.
04-19: She receives the Sacrament of Confirmation.
11-05: From Piacenza she writes to Sister Anne Battistina Bertuzzi telling her that, if they do not remove the quarantine, she would not be able to travel to Sicily.
11-06: The couple leaves for Marsalis. After being involved in financial difficulties, they are welcomed back home in Genoa by Rosa’s father.
She gives a conference to the sisters of Sampierdarena.
12-08: The birth of Carlotta who at early age becomes deaf and dumb.
She makes the perpetual vows of chastity and obedience.
She makes a perpetual vow of poverty.
With the vestition of the first five novices, the new Institute started officially its existence.
The first five dumb and deaf Tertiaries of St. Anne Perpetual Adorers receive the habit.
Monsignor Granito wrote the same request to the Pope.
The 25 years of the foundation of the Institute are complete. Cardinal Verga confers the veil on eight young novices.
11-28: She is in Sampierdarena; the birth of Alessandro.
She leaves for Florence, after the demand of Alessandro.
The Spiritual Exercises for the community begin. Chronology
12-01: While nursing a sick niece, the Servant of God tells a confidential matter to Sister Anne Celsa Speranza and stressing some actual sufferings, tells “Its 17 years that I lead this life of true martyrdom, but from the Feast of St. Anne onward I am fully abandoned.”
03-09: Gerolamo dies at the age of only 31 years old.
09-24: She professes as a Franciscan tertiary and chooses St. Francis as a special patron.
12-11: The Bishop of Acqui, Modesto Contratto, approves the Regulations for a new foundation under the title of the Immaculate Minims of St. Francis.
She writes from Bologna; she said: “For some time now it could be said that I am always on the railway.”
In the afternoon she leaves for
12-29: She leaves for Rome to meet Pope Pius IX.
01-01: She arrives in Rome together with her friend Teresa Porta, widow of Morasso. She had an extraordinary experience of the invisible stigmata.
Cardinal Verga visits the General House and takes to heart the Institute.
01-03: She has a private audience with Pius IX. The Pope orders her to found the Institute.
She writes from Rome. She is busy with the Rules and meeting with some prelates.
01-04: In the church of St. Marcello al Corso, she entrusts the children she must leave to the Virgin of Sorrows .
Sister Anne del Salvatore arrives in Naples; Mother Rosa leaves with her to Palermo.
Mother Rosa is in Naples, the first stage of her journey to Palermo.
01-22: She has another audience with Pius IX. She receives the Rewritten with the faculties for the Oratories of the future Institute.
She stays in Campania at least for eight days.
She leaves for S. Lucia. She gathers the superiors of the nearby houses. She visits Aci Sant’Antonio.
01-28: She returns to Genoa. She stops in Piacenza to negotiate the opening of the first house.
She gives a conference to the girls in the Mother House.
She arrives in Palermo and visits the eight houses of the city. She gathers the sisters in the nearby houses. She opens a house in Marsala.
03-13: She leaves her family (jumping over her mother’s body who is lying on the threshold to prevent her departure). She arrives in Piacenza with five companions to start the foundation of the Institute.

The General Council meets for the first time. The meeting was presided over by Cardinal Alimonda and by Monsignor Carlo Laurenzi. An act of submission was made to the Sacred Congregation. A decision was made to erect three Provinces and to transfer the General House to Rome.
03-25: She meets, for the first time, Father Giovanni BattistaTornatore, a Vincentian Missionary who will be the co-founder of the Institute.
03-26: She signs the contract for the purchase of the Palace Dal Verme in Stradone Farnese.
Scrive da Roma a mons. Vitelleschi chiedendo di affiancare al padre Fava altri due Consultori, e di reintegrare padre Tornatore nelle sue funzioni.
12-07: The new chapel is blessed and called it “of the Immaculate.”
The General Council sends a circular letter to the superiors to inform them concerning the accusations against Mother Rosa and to affirm her innocence.
02-02: She leaves for Cento (Ferrara) to start the new community in the hospital beside the “Concettini” brothers (after Concezionisti). Chronology
07-04: She leaves for Milan for the reception of Holy Communion of her daughter Carlotta.
07-26: On the feast of St. Anne she receives the religious habit, together with other twenty novices.
She celebrates solemnly the Feast of Chronology St. Anne during which three Bishops (of Piacenza, Osimo and Fidenza) participate.
For the feast of St. Anne, in the Mother House, in addition to Monsignor Scalabrini, Cardinal Alimonda, the Bishop of La Paz and that of Cremona are present.
The Decree of Approval of the Constitutions ad decennium is signed.
Si celebra il 25° dell’Istituto e il 25° di vestizione della Fondatrice. Vengono approvate definitivamente le Costituzioni. I festeggiamenti si protraggono per tre giorni.
She stays for the Feast of St. Anne in Florence but without staying for the night.
She celebrates the Feast of St. Anne in an extraordinary solemnity in the MEMOIRS religious rite as well as in the external preparation.
07-17: She sends the text of the Rule to the Holy Father and asks for his approval.
The Spiritual Exercises for the superiors of the Institute start.
She returns to Piacenza for the novena and Feast of St. Anne in which Cardinal Alimonda also participates.
11-14: She is in Sampierdarena for the opening of the house.
12-10: She gives a conference to the sisters of Sampierdarena.
She goes to Cortemaggiore (probably within the day).
02-14: She is present in the recognition of Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi in the cemetery of Sant’Orsola and she also signed the minutes. End of February She leaves for Rome and travels without stopping for 30 hours until Potenza. She then stops for 24 hours and leaves for Rome.
Bishop Scalabrini brought the blessing of Leo XIII to Alessandro and to Mother Rosa. Even the Pope exhorted her to nurse her son till the end.
03-31: She is called back to Piacenza because of the accusations made by the superior, Sister A. Maria Luigia Camisa.
She gives a conference on poverty to the sisters of Genoa.
She writes from Piacenza, where she stays until the month of June.
Good Friday. Mother Rosa is obliged by Cardinal Verga to spend the day with the community, instead of retiring in her room as she usually did. Chronology
04-15: She goes to Cento and remained there for two days.
She writes from Giugliano (Naples) where she attends the opening of the house. Chronology
05-04: The Bishop of Firenze Monsignor Eugenio Cecconi gives her an order to remove the sisters from Firenze.
She calls the sisters around her and thanks them. She asks for the Madonnina of Father Bernardo to be brought to her room and she wakes up to pray. At night she asks for Holy Communion as Viaticum.
05-09: She leaves for Piacenza. She stopped at Alessandria to negotiate with the prefect regarding the opening of the house of Nizza Monferrato.
She leaves for Messina. Her brother Francesco goes to meet her.
06-15: She writes from Ferrara. She is able to solve the problem of the house with the help of her brother Federico. Chronology
08-25: She goes to Sampierdarena where she remains there for ten days.
She returns to the Mother House, where about hundred sisters have concluded their Spiritual Exercises.
09-05: She returns to Piacenza and remains there until the end of the year. Beginning She goes to Sampierdarena. of January
She writes from Novi Ligure while traveling.
01-10: She writes from Genoa, in the house of her sick father where she stays there for six days.
She is in Rome, where she remains until the end of April to visit the nearby houses.
She leaves for Palermo and remains there until 8 February.
She goes to Conversano. Cardinal Sanfelice answers negatively to Monsignor Granito regarding the “Sons of St. Anne”.
The Cardinal Marian Rampolla is informed by the holy Father of being appointed Protector of the Institute.
01-16: She writes from Rome, where she remains for the whole month of April.
She starts the journey back and stops in Catania.
She arrives in Piacenza to visit her son, again being called by Bishop Scalabrini.
02-15: She writes from Sampierdarena where she assisted Sister Anne Blandina in her agony and death. Chronology
Mother Rosa receives a visit by Father Bernardino.
03-04: She has a private audience with Pius IX.
She is informed that the superiors of Pistoia and Prato have made a schism. She is forced to denounce them to the civil authorities for robbery.
04-08: She makes religious profession as a Daughter of St. Anne in the chapel of the Mother House.
She is present for the first Holy Communion of some girls of Sampierdarena.
The Decree of Approval of the Institute was granted.
With the investiture of the first novice, the novitiate is opened on D’Ossuna Street.
05-01: Her condition improves and attributes the healing to Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae.

The new church is dedicated to “Mary, Chronology Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae”. The rite is presided over by Cardinal Vicar Parocchi, who was assisted by Monsignor Bianchi and Monsignor Cassetta. The master of ceremonies is Monsignor Nazzareno Marzolini.
05-02: She has an aching arm. She informs Federico about having collected money for her sister Elisa, who is sick and without any help.
She asks for the removal of the chain of iron around her belt which hinders her breathing. Sister Serafina Foglia is forced to use pincers.
06-05: She writes from Pistoia to Princess Emilia of Fitalia.
09-25: She writes from Genoa where she stays until October 9.
10-10: She gives a conference to the sisters of the Mother House.
She writes from Ferrara, where she has arrived some days ago.
Within a day she goes to Borgo S. Donnino (Fidenza).
10-17: She gives a conference on the love of God to the novices, who desire to have a remembrance before her departure.
11-01: She gives a conference to the sisters of Sampierdarena. She travels to Nizza Monferrato to deal with the opening of the house.
Cardinal Verga takes possession of the Institute as its Protector.
11-22: She leaves for Rome. She stops in Firenze, since she is not yet well.
Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi writes telling her not to travel to Sicily until a new order, “because the good Lord wills it.”
She leaves for Piacenza, having been called by her son and by Bishop Scalabrini.
She writes to Emilia of Fitalia that she receives the visit of a Polish priest who comes from Chile and wanted to take the sisters to Poland. She stated: “He does not know that I know him for long.”
12-13: In a letter she speaks about the soup she is distributing to the poor.
01-29: She gives a conference to the community of the Mother House.

The visitator, Sister Anne Camilla Valentini, gives a report concerning Gargatano to the Prefect of the Sacred Congregation affirming that the superior Levi made the petition while being pushed by the parish priest of Sparavera, Father Costagnola.
02-04: She shares a meditation with the girls of Piacenza. She wrote from Sampierdarena.
02-10: She shares a meditation about the death of the sisters of Piacenza.
Informs the Count Caracciolo, who is preparing a golden frame for the small image of Father Bernardo.
Monsignor Cavicchioni accomplishes the first visit of the General House.
02-19: She shares a meditation about hell with the sisters of Piacenza.

She receives communication from Monsignor Wanstienkist that the Sacred Office has disapproved the Rules written by Father Tornatore and has ordered her to burn them and to distance the author from the Institute.
She arrives in Palermo where she stays for about two months.
02-21: She shares a meditation with the sisters of Piacenza.
Her niece Maria Adelaide is married to Duke Baldassarre Donati.
02-23: She shares a meditation with the sisters of Sampierdarena.
02-25: She gives a conference in Sampierdarena about the importance of keeping the Rule.
In her journey to Rome, she stops at Bologna at the Countess Trotti, who without reason insults her in front to many people.
02-26: She shares another meditation with the sisters of Sampierdarena.
She travels over the Adriatic line and stops in Ancona.
03-12: She gives a conference on poverty to the sisters of Sampierdarena.
While she is in Foligno, at night, some evil intentioned people put fire on the main door.
In a letter to Sister Anne Crocifissa Fiocchi, she communicated: “Friar Angelo is condemned in the prison of Firenze.”
She goes to Naples to visit the houses.
03-14: She gives a conference on the “Love of God” to the sisters of Sampierdarena.
03-20: She shares a meditation on the “Entrance of Jesus to Jerusalem” to the girls of Sampierdarena.
She is in Naples. She has a long conversation with Father Donato Giannotti.
03-29: She returns to Piacenza accompanied by Mrs. Rusca of Genoa.
04-17: She leaves for Genoa for the opening of the house of nurses for the sick at home in the house of Mrs. Rusca.
She is in Rome on Easter Sunday. Maria Teresa Patti of the Dukes of Sorrentino and Fanny Gregori receive the religious habit.
04-21: She writes from Sampierdarena. In Sampierdarena and Genoa she stays until 8 May.
The Decree of definitive Approval of the Institute is signed.
05-27: She left for Rome with Father Tornatore in order to present the Rules to the Sacred Congregation. She lodges in a family near the convent of the Minims: “St. Francis of Paola ai Monti.”
She writes from Filottrano. The following evening and morning she would be in Loreto in the Holy House.
She goes to Paris, where she is a guest of Arce, a Bolivian gentleman.
07-11: She writes from Piacenza. In this letter she informs Father Raimondo Bianchi that she stopped for eight days in Foligno; made stop-over in Firenze to negotiate the opening of the house; she stopped for two days with the Countess Trotti in Bologna and goes to Ferrara. She remains in Piacenza until the beginning of September.
10-04: In Genoa she has to swear in the cause of Ricchini. On account of her illhealth, she is interrogated in the house.
10-30: She writes from Piacenza. While returning, she stops in Bologna at the Countess Trotti.
Second session of the General Chapter.
11-04: Because of misunderstandings in her family, she is obliged to order her daughter to vacate the apartment next to the General House.
11-20: The first missionaries leave for Bolivia. She allowed herself to be photographed. She stays in Piacenza until the end of the year. She undertakes the visit of the houses nearby.
She has conversation with Father Donato Giannotti. She leaves for Cosenza, she reaches there on 21st.
11-23: She meets Alessandro whose condition has worsened. She would like to go to Berlin to consult a professor.
11-29: She spends the day in Florence. In the evening she leaves for Rome.
The Servant of God secretly communicates to Emilia of Fitalia that the new Protector of the Institute will be Chronology Cardinal Rampolla.
12-22: From Piacenza she writes to Monsignor Vitelleschi assuring him of her going to Rome for the well known question of the Rule.
She arrives in Rome. Cardinal Alimonda dissuades her from going to Sicily.
She leaves for Naples. The journey is uncomfortable; a small accident happens (cf. Memoirs of Sister Anne Celsa Speranza).
01-18: She is in Messina. She stays there for four days.
She arrives in Taranto and leaves for Bari.
02-05: She asks the Prefect of the Sacred Congregation to be allowed to welcome postulants, a prerogative which was suspended after the chapter of 1881. She informs him she will purchase a big building in Naples.
02-27: She arrives in Foligno and meets her friend Maria Grampini. On the same day she arrives in Rome and lodges with the Trevisani sisters (# 30 Sapienza Street).
Signs the contract for the purchase of the land for the construction of the General House.
02-29: She receives “the mortal blow”: the order not to communicate anymore with Father Tornatore. She has to Chronology write the Rules under the guidance of the Cardinal Protector who in turn delegates Monsignor Giordani, the Bishop of Ferrara.
03-10: She leaves for Ferrara and stops in Pesaro.
The new house on D’Ossuna Street purchased by Emilia of Fitalia and meant for school and novitiate is inaugurated.
She writes from Palermo, where she stays for about two months. Not being able to travel, she calls to herself all the sisters of the sixty houses of Sicily.
The health condition of the Servant of God becomes more uncertain.
03-11: Before reaching Ferrara she stops for some time in Bologna at the countess Trotti.
03-16: She has a conversation with Monsignor Giordani, who advises her to visit the houses in order to draw out the Rule from observance. The first Rule would be used for explanation.
In Piacenza her son Alessandro dies.
03-18: She leaves for Piacenza, where she stays for two days. On the journey she stops in Bologna at the Countess Trotti.

While the funeral of Alessandro is taking place in the Cathedral, Mother Rosa is busy in the Mother House for the farewell rite of the six sisters who are leaving for the new mission in New York with the missionaries of St. Carlo (Scalabrini). On the same evening she leaves for Rome.
She accepts in the Institute a sister of Sister Anne Francesca Camisa, because she owed much to that holy soul “who gave her life for the Institute”.
03-21: She leaves for Genoa to visit the houses of Genoa and Sampierdarena.
She visits the hospital of Frattamaggiore.
03-24: She gives a conference on humility and charity to the sisters of Genoa.
04-07: She is in Sampierdarena; she gives a conference to the sisters.
04-11: She leaves to visit Nizza Monferrato; she gives new impulse to the work of the sisters. She opens a school.
She writes from Rome. She thinks of leaving for Piacenza on April13. She gives news about the death of Cardinal Berardi.
04-16: She opens a house for the service of the maids.
Riceve la notizia della morte del conte Maurizio Caracciolo, benefattore dell’Istituto.
04-18: She leaves for Ferrara, where she starts writing the Constitutions. Cardinal Vannicelli tries to help her formulate them taking texts extracted from other already approved Constitutions as its base and to change the name of the Institute. The Servant of God opposes him decisively.

With a notary act, she annulls the papers signed in white which would have been used exclusively for the collections and not for the declaration of debts. In the afternoon she is visited by the Cardinal Protector, Rampolla. She assures him that the Institute is an unshakable rock and, after her death there will be no difficulties in governing it.
04-26: She hands over the Constitutions that she completes writing on the previous night.
She writes from Ferrara where she has just arrived. She must travel in search of collections.
She writes from Rome, where she has just arrived (according to a letter to Cardinal Celsia).
She assures Sister A. Celsa Speranza that, after her death her relatives would not raise any claim towards the Institute, which will have the special protection of Sister Anne del Salvatore.
05-28: She writes from Piacenza where she stays until August.
She writes about the brother of Emilia of Fitalia who dies on 30 January: “Tomorrow he will be freed and will go to heaven.”
05-29: She writes from Foligno. She plans to leave on May 30.
She writes from Paris and from Bordeaux. In this city she stays for few days.
06-13: She returns from Bologna to Ferrara.
She returns to Piacenza and stays there until the end of August.
She leaves for Piacenza and stays there until October.
In the Mother House she nurses Sister Anne Nazzarena Pastorini and mourns so much for her death.
She is in Naples. She receives a visit from Father Bernardino da Portogruaro. She remains there until June 17.
06-14: Cardinal Vannicelli sends to the Sacred Congregation the plan of the Constitutions written by Mother Rosa together with the negative opinion of Monsignor Giordani.
06-18: The Servant of God leaves Ferrara for Piacenza where she remains until August (with certainty until mid- August).
She writes from Bassano Veneto, where she stayed for eight days.
She leaves for Foggia on her way Loreto.
08-26: She writes from Ferrara where she goes for the examinations of the girls.
The controversy with Federico for the division of the property of the General House and of the cottage next to it is concluded.
08-31: Following the advice of the doctor, she goes to the “Colombarone”; at intervals she goes back to the Mother House.
09-09: She writes from Piacenza where she remains at least until 18 September.
For health reasons she goes to the “Colombarone”.
10-02: She goes to the Mother House for two days.
10-09: She returns to Piacenza where she stays until the end of February.
She writes to the Prefect of the Sacred Congregation that she is unable to go to Rome because she is sick.
The novitiate of Naples reopens with the investiture of five postulants.
10-15: She leaves for Firenze, where she stays for five days. She welcomes the Chronology superiors of the houses nearby. She meets Emilia of Fitalia as she returns to Palermo
She leaves for Rome without stopping anywhere.
She leaves for Rome accompanied by her doctor, Professor Lupi and Father Agostino Donadio.
10-24: She leaves for Sampierdarena, but soon returns to Genoa.
10-28: She leaves for Nizza, where she plans to stay for eight days.
12-16: She pleads with Monsignor Vitelleschi, Secretary of Bishops and Regular to give her back the sample of the Constitutions to be handed to Father Fava.
She leaves for Genoa, where her mother is dying. However she was Chronology called to Pisa and therefore she is unable to remain with her.
12-18: Monsignor Mariano Wanstienkist invites her to go to Rome in the following January (not before 10).
12-30: Within a day she visits the house of Monreale.
01-14: She leaves for Rome. She stops for the night in Bologna at the Countess Trotti.
She writes from Taranto, while traveling.
01-15: She arrives in Foligno for the opening of the house in the midst of many difficulties. The sisters arrive on January 20.
01-23: She leaves for Rome for the remaking of the Constitutions.
She leaves for Naples. She stops for some hours in S. Maria Capua Vetere.
She writes to Emilia of Fitalia, telling her of having “seen” her in bad mood. The Princess of Fitalia confirms that it is true.
02-06: In a letter to Sister Anne Giuseppa Troni, she approves that there should not be a solemn Mass for Father Tornatore.
02-08: She writes from Rome. They still try to change the name of the Institute.
02-16: She has an audience with Pius IX. The Pope confirms the name “Daughters of St. Anne.” Some premises in the monastery of Tor de’ Specchi are offered to her to open a school for poor girls.
04-05: She presents a text of Constitutions to the Sacred Congregation. She opens the school of “Parrocchietta”. Chronology
She receives the Holy Communion from the hands of the Pope in the Sistine Chapel.
10-05: She leaves for Rome because Federico is at his last breath.
The General Chapter is started and presided by Cardinal Protector Alimonda.
01-17: She receives the news of her father’s death.
The inauguration of the General House takes place; it is blessed by Cardinal Parocchi.

She leaves for Reggio Calabria. Her son Alessandro accompanied her because she receives threatening letters from Messina. The Mafia or Massons want to kill her. In this way the prophecy of Sister Anne del Salvatore has come true.
02-01: She has an audience with Pius IX.
A house is opened in Barcelona (Spain).
05-13: She writes from Falconara. She is traveling and stops in Bologna.
She goes to Torino to meet Cardinal Alimonda.
06-11: In Genoa, she receives some telegrams.
In the afternoon she goes to Cercola.
09-01: Following the advice of the doctor, she goes to Siena and remains there for twenty days.
09-14: She goes to Invorio Inferiore (Novara) to open a house.
09-18: She leaves for Nizza Monferrato. She plans to visit Bordighera and Ovada within ten days.
She writes from Bellinzago. She plans to visit even other houses.
04-03: While she is in Genoa, Sister Anne Vincenza Rapallino, her first secretary, dies in Piacenza.
Holy Thursday. The Queen Margaret and the Queen Mother are among the visitors of the church of the General House.
04-22: She calls the superior, sister Anne Carlotta Biagini, and reveals to her that she reads in her heart the plan of killing her.
05-31: She writes from Piacenza, where she stays until the beginning of September.
She leaves for Firenze. She thinks to visit the houses of Prato and Pistoia.
She is informed of the death of Cardinal Alimonda, Protector of the Institute.
06-01: In Piacenza, Monsignor Scalabrini crowns solemnly the image of Mary, Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae. On the same day the health condition of Sister Anne Francesca Savignone, superior of the Mother House, niece of Mother Rosa, worsens.
06-30: She writes from Piacenza where she stays until 7 August.
The Servant of God leaves for Florence.
08-10: She visits a Marian shrine in Ovada.
She goes to the countryside to the “Colombarone”.
The Protector, Cardinal Isidoro Verga, dies.
08-16: While in Naples, she receives news about the death of Sister Teofila, Provincial of the Sacramentines, as she predicted it on 6th.
09-08: Sister Anne Francesca Camisa and Sister Anne Angela Degrossi both die in the same house.
She writes to the foreign Minister who accepts the sending of the sisters to Assab. Chronology
09-15: She leaves the “Colombarone” definitively. The health conditions of her son Alessandro are getting serious.
11-13: Alessandro returns to Piacenza still decided to leave.
Arriva a Genova suor A. Giuseppa Troni proveniente dalla Bolivia con quattro novizie boliviane.
12-14: The Servant of God leaves for Rome and remains there until March.
04-13: She leaves for Genoa for the wedding of Carlotta.
04-20: The contract of dowry for Carlotta is signed.
04-27: The Servant of God leaves for Firenze where she stays for twenty days.
She leaves for Toscana. She stops for few hours at Orbetello.
05-19: She writes from Piacenza where she stays for 10 days.

She writes to Monsignor Scalabrini that she granted Sister Anne Candida Quadrani a permission to train in religious life his missionaries (the future Scalabrinian sisters); but for a limited period of time.
07-25: Cardinal Berardi arrives in Piacenza to celebrate the feast of St. Anne.
In Piacenza the first musical performance of the dumb and deaf is carried out in the presence of Cardinal Alimonda.
10-03: She goes to Naples with Cardinal Verga for the reopening of novitiate and the visit to the houses.
The Servant of God leaves for Florence.
10-19: She signs the agreement with Father Vincenzo Rocchi to send missionaries to Bolivia. Monsignor Scalabrini and Father Maurizio from Venezia are present. Chronology
She goes to Cercola for the inauguration of the new orphanage.
12-05: She leaves for Firenze and Pisa.
12-25: She writes from Rome, where she stays until April.
She goes to “Boccone del Povero” to distribute lunch to more than three hundred poor girls.
The Midnight Mass is celebrated in the chapel for the sake of the sick sisters, since she has obtained a special permission.
05-23: She goes to Appignano and Acquaviva Picena.
Blessing and placing of the first stone of the church by the Protector Cardinal Alimonda.
06-07: She writes from Piacenza, where she stays until the end of the year.
Sister Anne del Salvatore dies in Palermo.
She arrives at Lugo. She hopes to go to Loreto.
She leaves for Naples for the visit of the houses. She meets many superiors of the houses of southern Italy.
02-07: While she is in Spello she receives the news on the death of Pope Pius IX.
02-09: From Spello she returns to Rome.
From Palermo she leaves for Naples. She stops in Rossano to visit the hospital.
02-12: She goes to pay her last respect to Pius IX. She receives news that her son Alessandro was sick of tuberculosis.
04-23: She is in Firenze. She sends the superior Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi to Appignano.
She leaves for Rome through Ancona. She visits the Holy House of Loreto. On her journey she visits Ferrara, Bassano Veneto, and Legnano.

On Good Friday, Sister Anne Camilla Valentini enters in the room of the Servant of God and touching her shares the sufferings of the passion. Mother Rosa secretly tells her that she is suffering such pains for 28 years.
04-30: Writing to Sister Anne Maria Teresa Patti, she mentions: “The Institute is a rock! I look at it and in silence I place my head on it.”
05-08: From Piacenza she writes to Cardinal Alessandro Franchi, the new Protector of the Institute.
She writes from Piacenza to Bishop Scalabrini. She is happy if there would be sisters among the dumb and deaf ; she and the Institute are ready for his orders.
08-05: In Piacenza the Spiritual Exercises for the superiors start.
08-09: She writes from Piacenza, where she stays until the end of the year.
08-15: At the closure of the Spiritual Exercises she informs the superiors on the situation of the house of Firenze. Many proposed the expulsion of Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi while some asked to forgive her. She was forgiven.
The Spiritual Exercises in preparation of the General Chapter start in Piacenza. Mother Rosa gives a conference to the superiors on the everyday observance of the Rules.
01-09: She is urgently called to Rome by Alessandro who lost his job.
01-11: She writes from Acquaviva. She plans to go to Loreto, Appignano, Lugo and Ferrara; but she is forced to change her itinerary.
01-12: She writes from Rome and stays there until January 20. She thinks of going to Capua, Naples, and Cercola and, on her return, to pass through Foggia, with a short stay in Loreto, because of a vow she made.
She writes to Emilia of Fitalia that the appointment of the Protector aroused surprise since the Apostolic Visit is still in process.
02-22: Rientra a Piacenza. Si presume che nel viaggio di ritorno si sia fermata a Loreto.
In a letter she communicates that she has an audience with the Holy Father.
03-23: The Servant of God writes from Pistoia.
She is in Naples. She heals Sister Anne Fedele Santorelli from a grave illness.
06-02: Alessandro marries Vittoria Tellini. The Servant of God is present in the MEMOIRS matrimony which is celebrated in Rome.
06-12: She writes from Piacenza where she stays for many months.
She leaves for S. Maria Capua Vetere and visits the hospital. She takes time to talk with Father Donato Giannotti. She leaves for Naples.
01-13: She writes from Pistoia. She plans to go to Pisa from Jan 17-19.
01-30: She pleads with the Pope so that the election of the councilors may be done through a letter to the Cardinal Protector.
From Naples she goes to another place where a house is to be opened (probably the orphanage of Aversa).

She receives communication that Monsignor Beniamino Cavicchioni was nominated Delegate of the Protector of the Institute. It is an Apostolic Visit, in a veiled manner, following accusations that reached the Sacred Congregation.
04-24: She returns from Capua to Naples.
04-29: She is present when some novices receive the habit in Naples.
05-11: Mother Rosa is visited by Sister Savina Petrilli foundress of the Sisters of the Poor of St. Catherine of Siena.
The marble statue of Our Lady of Lourdes, which is venerated in the church, is crowned.
An agreement is signed with Gaspare Barbiellini Amidei to terminate the dispute started since July 1895.
05-12: She leaves from Rome and is on her way to France for the collection. She stops in Pisa for two days.
05-15: She pays back the visit of Sister Savina Petrilli.
08-30: She gives a speech to the community of the Mother House, who prepares a feast for her, exhorting them to faithfulness and attachment to Jesus the Crucified in difficulties. During this period she remains for long hours locked in her secret room.
03-05: She writes to her daughter: “Today the congress was very easy… everything is ended.”
03-19: She writes from Naples. On March 26 she would return to Rome.
She miraculously heals Sister Anne Paola Materazzo by anointing her with the oil of the Eternal Father.
She visits the house of Cercola.
04-02: From Piacenza she goes to Fiorenzuola d’Arda in the area of Gallo with her niece Maria Adelaide in order to rescue her from the epidemic from which the younger niece called “Rosetto” died. She stays in Fiorenzuola until 21 April.
06-19: She writes from Firenze. She plans to travel to Rome, on the following day.
06-26: She is in Piacenza. In a letter to Emilia of Fitalia she said: “A good soul who has much communication with Sister Anne del Salvatore has asked her if the punishment will come upon Palermo, if the cholera will come again. She says that this was the answer: ‘it will not come at all.’
08-23: The First General Chapter is celebrated in the presence of Monsignor Scalabrini, Bishop of Piacenza. The capitulars refuse most of the animadversiones of the Sacred Congregation, not knowing that this is an act of disobedience.
10-06: She is called to Rome to give an account of the acts of the Chapter.
She definitively leaves “Colombarone” to return to Piacenza.
11-16: Again she is called to Rome through Monsignor Scalabrini. Chronology
She has a long conversation with Father Bernardino da Portogruaro.
12-03: She goes to the Prefect of the Sacred Congregation. She is treated very severely. She has a number of meetings with different prelates and with Monsignor Carlo Laurenzi who, together with Cardinal Alimonda, takes care of the Institute in the following months.
03-03: She arrives in Rome. For a vow she made she calls for a solemn triduum of thanksgiving to the Blessed Trinity for the gifts granted to Sister Anne del Salvatore. She works for the dedication of the new church.
03-15: Second meeting of the General Council. They proceeded to make appointments for the different tasks. The Council makes a request to be received by the Holy Father and by Cardinal Prefect before leaving Rome.

The Spiritual Exercises for the superiors preached by Fr. Luigi Costantini start in the new house. Mother Rosa and Father Tornatore give an input every day. Some norms were established. These Spiritual Exercises are erroneously called Chapter.
After conferring with the Bishop of Aversa concerning the house of S. Antimo, she goes to visit Marcianise.
12-17: She writes from Pisa. On 18 December she would go to Siena. She receives the news of her mother’s death.
She is informed of the death of Father Cirillo, confessor of the Count Caracciolo (letter of Count Caracciolo of 18 December).
01-05: In a letter she tells that on January 9 she would travel to Rutigliano (Bari) and then to Messina.
She leaves Naples and stopped in Foggia.
02-03: She returns to Rome to follow up the building of the General House and of the church.

The lawyer Rosati, attorney of Maria Tellini, goes to the General House to pawn some of its furnitures in compensation for the expenses of the legal proceedings, though the house was not registered to the Foundress.
02-13: She writes from Naples. She foresees herself being in Rome on February 17.
She has an audience with the Holy Father.
02-20: Mother Rosa writes to Emilia of Fitalia that she did not understand well whether St. Joseph will take Alessandro before the month of his feast day.
03-01: She writes from Foligno. She is leaving for Orbetello, where she plans to stop for two days.
03-02: She writes from Naples, the first stage of her journey to Sicily.
03-07: She writes from Piacenza, where she had just arrived.
09-06: She writes from Rome. One of her brothers was sick.
09-11: She writes from Piacenza, where she stays until around the end of
She returns to the Mother House.
She leaves for Naples, where she stays for about a month.
11-19: Suor A. Giuseppa Troni arriva a Piacenza.
She goes to S. Maria Capua Vetere
01-20: She writes to Sister Anne Giuseppa Troni asking her to take the sisters for vaccination for smallpox, which is infecting Piacenza.
She leaves for Rome; she reaches there on 21st morning.
Maria Tellini the wife of the deceased Alessandro enters into the room of Mother Rosa in Piacenza by force expecting to find money.
05-14: She returns to Piacenza late in the evening.
06-24: Sister Anne Francesca Savignone dies in a state of great virtue. She is assisted by Mother Rosa.
06-25: The Servant of God confidentially tells Sister Anne Benedetta Carrega of having received signs foretelling an epidemic (cf. Memoirs of Sister Anne Celsa Speranza).
Father Bernadino da Portogruaro comes and stays for two days in the Mother House.
10-22: She invites the Princess of Fitalia in Piacenza. Sister Anne del Salvatore MEMOIRS will still remain for some days.
12-15: In the evening she leaves for Rome.
02-11: She reaches Naples and she stays there until 18.
02-18: She writes from Rome. She is busy for the building of the General House and with the Constitutions.
05-06: She sleeps in the Lord at 9:15 am while the bells of the church ring for the Feast.
06-06: She receives news on the worsening health of Sister Anne del Salvatore.
She leaves for Piacenza. She is called back to Italy because an order was given to close the house of Ferrara.
06-09: She writes in a letter regarding Sister Anne del Salvatore: “The sorrow is so much, the immense loss, irreparable. The plans of God are inscrutable. I would like to have words of consolation for you, but the grief prevents me.”
07-29: Sister Anne Camilla Valentini, Provincial of Bolivia, arrives in Piacenza.
She is leaving for Pisa, where she stays for two days.
The Visitator listens to the sisters of the Mother House. In the following days he visits Gargatano and the Institute of the dumb and deaf.
10-07: She returns to Piacenza because she forgot a credit paper in her room. Federico’s health is improving.

The second session of the Chapter takes place. Sister Vittoria Archetti, who arrives from Brazil, joins the other MEMOIRS superiors. In the documents there is neither a hint about Father Tornatore’s presence nor a record on the decision to distance him from the Institute.
She goes to Naples with Cardinal Verga.
10-23: She leaves for the visit of the houses starting from Toscana (letter of 22 October to Monsignor Briuccia).
10-29: The first session of the General Chapter is presided by Cardinal Verga.
11-21: Her brother Federico celebrates religious matrimony.
04-09: She communicates to Emilia of Fitalia foreseeing an epidemic in Palermo.
06-22: From Piacenza she writes to Emilia of Fitalia that on the 1st of July a house will be opened in Messina, according to a prophecy of Sister Anne del Salvatore.
She goes to Lodi where she stays for two days.
07-05: She writes from Piacenza. She prepares the departure of the sisters to Assab. Chronology
11-03: She writes from Rome and stays there the whole of February.
12-06: Monsignor Gennaro Granito di Belmonte has a private audience and asks the Pope to establish the “Sons of St. Anne”. Pope Leo orders him to put his inspiration into writing.
She leaves for Siena, where she will celebrate the Feast of the Immaculate Conception.
She shares with Sister Anne Giuseppa Troni her pain about the physical and spiritual health of Alessandro.
01-06: She goes to Lucera. Monsignor Granito asks Cardinal Sanfelice to establish the “Sons of St. Anne”.
01-08: The Servant of God goes to Bari.
She is informed that Sister Anne Zoe` Levi, superior of Gargatano, sends a petition to the holy Father.
01-25: She goes to Cataina. She was sick.
She has a visit by Father Bernardino da Portogruaro.
07-27: She leaves Rome and plans to visit Toscana.
She goes to Frascati to take a rest and stays there for eighteen days, but without any benefit.
Though she is suffering extremely, she remains in Rome for forty hours. Her health is declining more and more every day.
07-31: She leaves for Venezia in the evening and was called by Cardinal Patriarch Agostini. She goes to visit mother Anna Marovich.
The Princess of Fitalia comes to Piacenza.
She tells to Sister Anne Maria Teresa Patti, General Councilor the words of the Visitator: “You go ahead until we meet in Rome.” Chronology
She leaves for Liguria and stops in Pisa for two days.
10-20: She leaves from Firenze to Filottrano.
09-16: In the evening she leaves from Piacenza for Prato. She stays there for two days.
09-23: The Spiritual Exercises start in preparation for the General Chapter. Mother Rosa gives a conference every day to the superiors. There are 179 superiors present.
10-08: The capitulars are received by Pope Leo XIII. Mother Rosa remains in Rome for some months.
03-22: In the early morning she goes to the sanctuary of Pompei. She remains there because Bartolo Longo wanted to speak with her. She goes to Nola to visit the hospital and the orphanage.
03-30: The Secretary of Propaganda Fide presses her not to send her sisters to Luxor, as requested by the Affairs of Foreign Ministry.
06-21: In the morning she arrives in Piacenza and goes to the house of Count Caracciolo to visit Father Tornatore who is sick.
07-01: Start of the Spiritual Exercises under the guidance Father Carlo Amirante.
07-24: Cardinal Alimonda arrives in Piacenza for the Feast of St. Anne. Having found the Servant of God very sick, he orders her to go somewhere to rest.
08-06: She tells her secretaries confidentially that a Sacramentine Sister, “a holy soul,” will die.
08-12: From Sezze she goes to Bistagno.
08-14: She writes from Sampierdarena and she remains there for three days.
10-21: The Spiritual Exercises in preparation of the Chapter begin.
11-25: She leaves for Reggio Calabria; she stops for the night.

She informs her councilors that there were charges made against her. The accusations are regarding the use of Chronology goods, the collection of the Institute and the lack of means in the houses, for which the sisters also lack the basic necessities.
11-26: She arrives in Messina where she stays for five days.
Monsignor Gennaro Granito di Belmonte is appointed Apostolic Nuncio of Brussels. He is consecrated a Bishop in the church of the General House by Cardinal Rampolla.
06-04: Father Tornatore arrives to take part in the General Chapter of his Congregation. He visited Mother Rosa and spends most of the day in prayer Chronology before the Madonnina of Father Bernardo.
Her brother Federico is gravely sick. The wife prevents Mother Rosa from speaking to him about religion and the sacraments.
06-28: She starts a three day spiritual retreat.
She leaves for Florence. She stops for a few days because of sickness.
07-09: She writes from Piacenza. She is cured by quinine. She is very weak.
11-12: Her son is gravely sick and desires to see her. The Servant of God would like to make a sacrifice not to see him anymore and, in the following days, she writes exhorting him for resignation.
The Servant of God starts three days of spiritual retreat.
12-28: She starts writing the history of the Institute in an allegorical form. The Chronology work will be published with the title Travagli e Conforti.
07-06: The appointment of Cardinal Isidoro Verga as Protector of the Institute is announced.
She receives a visit of Bishop Monsignor Tommaso Reggio, who is promoted to the See of Archbishop of Genoa.
08-02: She writes from Genoa, where she stays for four days. She has a long conversation with Father Giuseppe Firpo her first confessor.
She leaves for Ovada and stays in the Hospice of Lercaro for about twenty days.
08-07: She writes from Sestri Ponente, where she stays for nine days.
05-03: Mother Rosa is interrogated at length in court for the cause of food promoted by her daughter-in-law Maria Tellini.
07-19: Cardinal Parocchi consecrates the new MEMOIRS major altar of the church, a gift for the 25th anniversary of the investiture of Mother Rosa. The work is done because of the concern of Cardinal Verga. The 25th Anniversary of the Foundation 26 July of the Institute and of the investiture of the Foundress are celebrated. The Constitutions are definitively approved. The celebrations are prolonged for three days.
In Piacenza, Gaspare Barbiellini takes his family back home but insists on his demands.
10-18: She returns to Rome, where she stays for a long time.
Parte per Firenze. Si ferma alcuni giorni.
09-20: She goes to Florence for six days.
09-26: She goes to Pistoia. She also meets the sisters of Prato and listens to them.
12-26: She goes to Naples, the first stage of her journey to Sicily.
03-06: Monsignor Gaetano Briuccia, a great benefactor of the Institute, dies in Palermo.
04-10: She leaves for Reggio Calabria, where she stays for 24 hours.
The Spiritual Exercises for the superiors begin. Mother Rosa gives a conference every day.
04-12: She arrives in Cosenza and visits the houses.
05-10: A hospital is opened in Nice (France).
A rebellion breaks out in Messina; soon her brother sets her off for Naples.
11-07: From Piacenza she leaves for Florence. Chronology
01-31: Father Giovanni Battista Tornatore dies in Piacenza.
05-07: Father Bernardino da Portogruaro dies. The community is informed on the 15th.
07-13: In a letter to Monsignor Granito di Belmonte, she said that the Barbiellini uses Carla as a hostage. The condition of her daughter prevents her from acting as she should, with the necessary energy.

Following the insistence of her doctor, she goes to Toscana in the municipality of Fiesole in the locality of S. Domenico, where her brother Francesco has rented for her the country-house of Pantellini.
01-24: The last child of Carlotta, Bernardo, is born.
08-04: She sees signs of an epidemic (in a letter to Monsignor Granito of 4 August and to Emilia of Fitalia of 6 August).
09-02: The process of beatification of Sister Anne del Salvatore Orsi starts in Palermo.
09-27: She writes in Naples, where she goes directly from Fiesole without stopping anywhere.
07-28: The Apostolic Visitator, Domenico Serafini, a Benedictine presents himself in the General House without any prior notice.
01-07: The Visitator examines the countability of the Institute.
09-03: She writes from Sampierdarena. She stays there with certainty until 24.
10-12: At night she has a heart attack.
05-05: Soon after midnight, Father Agostino Donadio brings for her the Viaticum. Towards the evening she wakes up from the bed for a while to pray to the “Madonnina”. At 21 o’clock she is given the Sacrament of the Sick by Father Vincenzo da Alatri.
Verso sera si alza qualche momento dal letto per pregare la “Madonnina”. Alle 21 le viene amministrata l’Estrema Unzione da padre Vincenzo da Alatri.
